subject: DPIA exhibits, Art 28/30 ledger excerpt and subprocessor matrix — Novamed compliance pack
content:
--- Message 1 (external) ---
From: Lena Møller <lena.moller@novamed.dk>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Novamed Legal <novamed-legal@novamed.dk>
Cc: Pierre Dubois <p.dubois@novamed.dk>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Request: DPIA exhibits + Art. 28/30 ledger excerpt for upcoming internal review

Hannah / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our internal privacy review flagged a couple of items they need before we can sign off on procurement: a copy of the Article 30 processing ledger excerpt relevant to Novamed, the latest subprocessor inventory with data locations (EU/US/APAC), and a KMS attestation showing customer key separation (or note if using provider-managed keys).

Specifically we need: 
- Article 30 ledger excerpt that shows processing activities, categories of data, and subprocessors that touch Novamed data.
- A CSV subprocessor matrix export with columns: Name, Role, Processing Type, Data Residency, Contracted Data Transfer Mechanism (e.g., SCCs, BCR, adequacy).
- Any attestation around encryption/KMS (txt/pdf).
- Clarification on the cross-border transfer mechanism (are we relying on SCCs for EU->US subprocessors or another mechanism?).

Can we have these by EOD Monday (24 Jul)? Our legal team will insert them into the DPIA package and we can move to the next procurement gate.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Møller
Head of Privacy, Novamed A/S

--- Message 2 (internal reply) ---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Møller <lena.moller@novamed.dk>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 13:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA exhibits + Art. 28/30 ledger excerpt for upcoming internal review

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. We can assemble these but want to confirm a few quick items so we deliver the correct scope: 

1) Article 30 ledger excerpt: do you want a filtered PDF showing only entries that mention Novamed project IDs (you referenced HS-CRM-112233 in the intake), or a CSV export of all processor activities where we highlight the relevant lines? We can do both but prefer to know which is needed for your DPIA insert.

2) Subprocessor matrix: we can produce subprocessor_matrix_v3.csv (includes data residency and contract transfer mechanism). We'll call out which subprocessors are hosted in the US and which use SCCs. Note that a small set of telemetry processors are EU-only.

3) KMS attestation: we have a short KMS key separation attestation (kms_key_attestation.txt) and a redacted example of our key policy. If you require a signed letter on company letterhead, we will route to Legal and need +48 hours.

4) Cross-border transfers: our default is SCCs for EU->US subprocessors; for a subset of partners we rely on adequacy decisions or customer-chosen on-prem / VPC deployments. We will include a transfer_mechanisms summary sheet.

Action plan: Irene will assemble the ledger excerpt and subprocessor matrix. Marissa will pull the KMS attestation and SCC inventory. Karthik will add a short note on contract status and whether subprocessors are included in our DPA (Art. 28 clauses).

We should be able to get the initial pack to you by EOD Monday but if you need a letterhead-signed attestation faster, let us know now so we can escalate.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 (external clarification) ---
From: Novamed Legal <novamed-legal@novamed.dk>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Møller <lena.moller@novamed.dk>, Pierre Dubois <p.dubois@novamed.dk>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:21:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA exhibits + Art. 28/30 ledger excerpt for upcoming internal review

Thanks Hannah — CSV exports are ideal for our DPIA template. A filtered Article 30 CSV that shows only activities tied to HS-CRM-112233 would be perfect. 

Regarding signatures: a company-letterhead attestation would be preferred but is not mandatory for the first pass; PDF attestation is fine for now as long as it includes the date and the signatory name/role.

Also two small follow-ups: 
- Can you include the last 90 days of subprocessor access logs for the top three subprocessors (redacted to account IDs only)? If that's not possible, a sampling note describing access control frequency is acceptable.
- For SCCs: if any subprocessor relies on a derogation (e.g., an alternative transfer mechanism), please flag it in the CSV and note the fallback.

We appreciate the fast turnaround. If Monday EOD is tight, Tuesday morning CET is acceptable.

Regards,
Novamed Legal Team

--- Message 4 (internal consolidated response & attachments) ---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Novamed Legal <novamed-legal@novamed.dk>, Lena Møller <lena.moller@novamed.dk>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 18:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA exhibits + Art. 28/30 ledger excerpt for upcoming internal review

Hi Lena / Novamed team — attaching the initial compliance pack below. Per your preference we include CSV extracts and short, signed-style attestations (PDF/TXT). We also added a short transfer mechanisms workbook that flags any deviating transfer approaches. Please review and confirm whether you want the full (unredacted) subprocessor access logs — that requires a Data Access review and we would provide a secure, time-limited S3 share if approved.

Attachments (stubs attached here):
- redwood_article30_ledger_excerpt.pdf (filtered to HS-CRM-112233; shows purposes, categories, subprocessors)
- subprocessor_matrix_v3.csv (Name | Role | Processing Type | Data Residency | Transfer Mechanism | DPA Art. 28 included)
- kms_key_attestation.txt (dated 2028-07-19; includes signatory name and key separation statement)
- sccs_and_transfer_mechanisms.xlsx (summary sheet that flags SCC usage and adequacy references)

Quick notes: 
- We flagged three subprocessors that currently rely on SCCs for EU->US transfers; these are marked in the CSV column "Transfer Mechanism". 
- The telemetry vendors are EU-only and therefore show EU residency. 
- If you want last-90-days access logs for top subprocessors, confirm a secure transfer mechanism (we prefer an S3 pre-signed URL with limited TTL and an NDA addendum).

Next steps proposed: 
1) Novamed confirms whether CSV + PDF pack satisfies the DPIA intake (target: Mon 23 Jul). 
2) If Novamed requires signed-on-letterhead attestation, we will escalate to Legal (ETA 48 hours). 
3) Schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through flagged subprocessors (Irene to propose times).

Thanks — the pack is attached here and we stand by for questions.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment stubs --
redwood_article30_ledger_excerpt.pdf (application/pdf; 120 KB)
subprocessor_matrix_v3.csv (text/csv; 24 KB)
kms_key_attestation.txt (text/plain; 3 KB)
sccs_and_transfer_mechanisms.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet; 45 KB)

-- End of thread --
